# Requirements

Turn the v10 fleet primitives into a system a team can hand a spec to and leave running for days: a durable, crash-resumable, three-level supervisor that runs features, managers, and workers concurrently and manages every Codex or Claude Code process until its work is merged; agents briefed from the graph instead of from prose; drift caught across branches before it merges; and an editor that shows all of it live over one push connection, with Start, steering, and approvals in the chat.

## Requirement 1: Durable three-level fleet supervisor

**User Story:** As the owner of a multi-day project, I want to press Start on a spec and have the main agent, a manager per feature, and workers per task created and supervised until every task is qualified and merged, surviving crashes and restarts, so that nobody has to babysit the processes.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN cg fleet up starts a run THE supervisor SHALL persist the run, every node (role, parent, agent, task, branch, worktree, pid, attempt, fence, retries, spend), and every transition in the database, and WHEN the supervisor restarts with --resume THE run SHALL continue from that state without re-spawning live children or forgetting retry counts.
2. WHEN the run starts THE supervisor SHALL spawn a real main agent process, one feature manager per feature whose requires are met, and workers under each manager, so that several features progress at the same time.
3. WHEN a manager and its workers are live at once THE merge of a worker's branch into the feature worktree SHALL be serialized by a merge lock instead of by the two levels taking turns.
4. WHEN several tasks of one wave have disjoint declared touches and no predicted collision THE supervisor SHALL run them on separate task branches in parallel, bounded by the role's concurrency limit.
5. WHEN workflow.kvx declares [role.*] capabilities THE supervisor SHALL honour each role's driver, model, extra args, concurrency limit, wall-clock budget, and spend budget.
6. WHEN cg fleet down, pause, or resume runs THE supervisor SHALL drain, freeze, or continue the run gracefully, releasing claims on drain and keeping branches.
7. WHEN workflow.kvx declares an approval gate on land, pr, retry-exhausted, or drift THE supervisor SHALL stop at that point and emit an approval request instead of proceeding, and SHALL proceed only on an explicit approve.

## Requirement 2: Supervision that notices, retries, and escalates

**User Story:** As the fleet owner, I want a stuck, looping, or failing agent to be noticed and handled automatically so that one bad process cannot stall a multi-day run.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN a live worker makes no progress (no new file change, commit, tool call, or spec transition) within the stall window THE supervisor SHALL send a nudge, and WHEN the next window also passes without progress THE supervisor SHALL terminate it and restart it with a handoff, instead of renewing its heartbeat forever.
2. WHEN a worker exceeds its wall-clock or spend budget THE supervisor SHALL stop it, record why, and treat the attempt as failed.
3. WHEN an attempt fails THE supervisor SHALL retry the task up to the role's retry limit with the Jev triage, the verify_cmd tail, and the previous attempt's summary in the new prompt.
4. WHEN retries are exhausted THE task SHALL be escalated to its manager, then to the main agent, and WHEN still unresolved it SHALL be marked blocked with the reason while the rest of the run continues.
5. WHEN any child exits THE outcome SHALL be decided by the task's status on the branch tip and the merge state, never by the exit code alone.

## Requirement 3: Graph-grounded agent context

**User Story:** As a worker agent, I want my briefing built from the graph (the code I will touch, what my upstream tasks actually produced, and what my siblings are changing) so that I start oriented instead of rediscovering the repository.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN a worker is spawned THE prompt SHALL contain a task packet built from the graph within a token budget: the task's criteria, the current definitions of its declared symbols, their callers and callees, the symbols its required tasks actually introduced on the feature branch with signatures, relevant memories, and the touches of live sibling workers.
2. WHEN upstream work merges into the feature branch while a worker runs THE next cg work update SHALL report the merged symbols and changed signatures as a delta.
3. WHEN a manager is woken THE prompt SHALL contain the subtree state, open conflicts, failed attempts with triage, pending approvals, and drift findings for its feature.
4. WHEN the retrieval evaluation runs THE task packets for the fixture tasks SHALL reach the recorded recall threshold for their gold symbols and SHALL stay inside the budget.

## Requirement 4: Drift caught across the fleet

**User Story:** As a reviewer of a million-line project built by agents, I want every place the work drifts from the spec, or from another branch, flagged before it merges so that the drift never reaches main unnoticed.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN a task is qualified or merged up THE diff SHALL be compared with the task's declared symbols and touches, and public symbols changed outside the declaration SHALL be reported as spec drift.
2. WHEN a merge into a feature branch changes the signature or removes a symbol that another live branch references THE affected workers and their managers SHALL receive an interface-drift event naming the symbol, the old and new signature, and the referencing sites.
3. WHEN the supervisor picks tasks to run in parallel THE tool SHALL predict collisions from declared touches and the call graph impact of declared symbols, and SHALL serialize predicted collisions instead of running them together.
4. WHEN a feature is about to land THE tool SHALL report every acceptance criterion that is not traced to a qualified task with evidence.
5. WHEN drift is found THE finding SHALL be recorded as an event and surfaced in brief, fleet tree, and the editor, SHALL warn by default, and SHALL block only where workflow.kvx opts in.

## Requirement 5: Live event stream and cg serve

**User Story:** As an interface built on Codify, I want one long-lived connection that answers any command and pushes every change as it happens so that nothing has to poll.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN any fleet or spec state changes (task status, claim, attempt, spawn, exit, stall, retry, escalation, merge, gate, pull request, drift, approval) THE change SHALL be appended to an events table with a monotonic sequence number, kind, subject, and JSON payload.
2. WHEN a client runs cg serve THE server SHALL speak newline-delimited JSON-RPC over stdio, answer every tool the MCP server exposes, and push subscribed events from a given sequence number within 250 ms of their commit.
3. WHEN a child agent runs under a driver with structured output THE supervisor SHALL parse its stream (text, tool calls, tokens, cost) into agent events, and SHALL keep the raw log on disk.
4. WHEN cg serve is idle THE server SHALL NOT hold the write lock or run index passes.
5. WHEN cg events --follow runs THE command SHALL stream the same events as text or JSON for terminal users.

## Requirement 6: Real-time editor that exposes the whole fleet

**User Story:** As a developer, I want to start, watch, steer, and approve the whole fleet from the editor, with views that keep up in real time and a chat that reaches every capability Codify and its agents have.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN the extension connects to a cg that supports serve THE extension SHALL use one serve connection for every call and event, SHALL update views incrementally from events within 300 ms, and SHALL NOT poll; WHEN the binary is older THE extension SHALL fall back to the v10 behaviour.
2. WHEN the user presses Start on a feature (CodeLens on the spec, view title, or chat) THE extension SHALL show the plan (roles, agents, branches, parallel groups, predicted collisions, budgets), and on confirm SHALL run cg fleet up, with Stop, Pause, and Resume available while it runs.
3. WHEN the fleet view renders THE tree SHALL show main, managers, and workers live with state, task, current step, last output line, tokens and cost, stall and retry indicators, and SHALL open an agent's live transcript on click.
4. WHEN the chat is used THE slash commands SHALL be generated from the served tool list so that every Codify capability is reachable, the chat SHALL attach to any fleet agent's live transcript and send it a steering message, and approval requests and escalations SHALL appear inline as actionable cards.
5. WHEN a transcript or event list holds ten thousand entries THE webview SHALL stay responsive through windowed rendering, measured headlessly.

## Requirement 7: Qualified at fleet scale

**User Story:** As the team trusting Codify with a multi-day run, I want proof that the whole life cycle works under failure, not just on the happy path.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN the fleet end-to-end fixture runs with a scripted fake driver across two features with a failing task, a stalling worker, a merge conflict, and an interface change THE run SHALL finish with every task qualified and merged, the pull requests opened through a fake gh, the retry, stall restart, conflict report, and interface-drift event all recorded.
2. WHEN the supervisor is killed in the middle of that run and restarted with --resume THE run SHALL still complete with the same result.
3. WHEN v11 is released THE documentation SHALL describe the supervisor, roles, supervision, context packets, drift, serve, and the editor, with their limitations.
